A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UnInfo research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original prompting experiments, adaptation benchmarks, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark, model, severity, continual-adaptation, and ablation experiments, including Appendix E.

M1.justification: The proposed UnInfo algorithm retains the same entropy and uniformity losses, mutual-information-based balancing, image-encoder LoRA updates, EMA distillation, and teacher inference. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix B. Newly evaluated alternative losses and parameter updates are experimental ablations, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR10-C and CIFAR100-C, lower ImageNet-C corruption severities, and sequential corruption streams for continual adaptation. These substantially broaden the represented data and input conditions. ImageNet and ImageNet-A/R already appeared in v1; their additional adaptation results do not introduce new datasets.

E2.justification: DMN, Mint, and BATCLIP enter the retained ImageNet-C/C-bar comparisons and efficiency table in v2. DMN was previously discussed but not evaluated. Mint and BATCLIP provide competing encoder-updating approaches absent from v1's comparisons; Appendix E.6 additionally evaluates BATCLIP with LoRA.

E3.justification: The stated main checkpoint changes from DataComp-1B in v1 Section V-B to LAION-2B in v2 Section 5.2. Identical retained benchmark means do not establish whether experiments were rerun. New evaluation configurations include OpenAI ViT-B/32, SigLIP, and continual adaptation without resets using learning rate 0.0001.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations and sensitivity plots, v2 tests mutual-information objectives, fixed versus dynamic balancing, batch size, encoder versus embedding updates, and LoRA versus LayerNorm with teacher controls. Appendix E also adds hyperparameter-selection checks, continual-adaptation analysis, and prediction-imbalance analysis of collapse.

E5.justification: v2 adds per-result ± uncertainty values throughout the primary accuracy and ablation tables, where v1 reported means alone. Both versions already specify three random-seed runs and include uncertainty in some efficiency/sensitivity displays; no increase in runs is established. The accuracy tables do not clearly identify what their ± quantities represent.

E6.justification: Shared primary benchmark means remain unchanged, including UnInfo's 27.10% and 36.13%. Added Mint results of 29.14% and 38.06% remove UnInfo's leading average ranking. Entropy-only ablation means change from 0.10% on both datasets to 0.22% and 0.29%. The Gaussian-noise weight trajectory changes in Figure 3→4, and extensive additional benchmark and analysis results appear.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the data-processing argument: v1 treats H(Z|X) as constant because the encoder is deterministic; v2 instead explicitly assumes small fluctuations and describes decreasing embedding entropy as likely. This changes the mathematical assumptions and reasoning without introducing a new theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: v2 drops the introduction's assertion that corruption adaptation for VLMs has not been explored and reframes the problem around domain-shift methods' over-specialization. The central contribution remains UnInfo's uniformity-aware, information-balanced encoder adaptation; its three main components and headline accuracy-improvement claim are retained.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges that regularized mutual-information optimization can rival UnInfo and attributes improvements to combined components rather than uniformity alone. It adds substantive qualifications concerning small-batch estimation, i.i.d. sampling, continual-adaptation interference, and the confounded encoder-versus-embedding ablation. Performance discussion shifts toward consistency relative to No-adapt despite stronger competitors.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an exact pretrained-checkpoint link, names the four tuning corruptions, explains clean-data-based threshold selection, and explicitly documents once-per-sample batched evaluation. Appendix D specifies spherical transport costs and the POT implementation for the existing EMD analysis. Most optimizer settings and the existing code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning by adding encoder-updating corruption methods such as Mint, BATCLIP, CLIPArTT, and WATT, including Mint's conceptual relationship to uniformity. Related work is organized along episodic/cumulative and frozen/updating-encoder axes, replacing v1's predominantly frozen-encoder comparison narrative.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much existing exposition remain recognizable. v2 condenses the abstract, edits and expands explanations, consistently substitutes image corruption for sensor degradation, reorganizes related-work paragraphs, swaps qualitative and efficiency subsections, and relocates pseudocode into the expanded appendix.

P2.justification: The document changes from an IEEE-style two-column layout to a single-column format. Tables are extensively reformatted with angled headers and uncertainty entries, sensitivity panels become side by side, and numerous experimental tables and analysis plots are added. The original overview and embedding visualization remain, while the weight-trajectory figure is revised.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a major weakness of v1's evidence by comparing against competing encoder-updating methods and testing broader datasets, models, and failure conditions. The additional loss and parameter ablations, uncertainty reporting, and explicit limitations substantially strengthen assessment of when and why UnInfo works. Remaining problems include the unexplained checkpoint-description change and overbroad superiority wording: BATCLIP does not exceed UnInfo on ImageNet-C-bar, despite the accompanying generalization.
